description: Validate and sanitize every user input at the boundary
rationale: Unvalidated input is the root of injection and deserialization attacks

description: Use parameterized queries or ORM bindings, never concatenation
rationale: Concatenated SQL enables classic injection attacks

description: Never commit secrets, tokens, or keys — use env vars or secret managers
rationale: Committed secrets persist in git history and leak via CI

description: Hash passwords with bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2id — never MD5 or SHA-1
rationale: Fast hashes allow offline cracking of leaked databases

description: Use short-lived access tokens (<= 15 min) with refresh rotation
rationale: Short TTL limits the blast radius of a stolen token

description: Enforce CSRF tokens or SameSite=strict cookies on state-changing requests
rationale: Cookie auth is vulnerable to CSRF without explicit protection

description: Escape user-controlled content in HTML and attribute contexts
rationale: Unescaped output is the primary XSS vector
CSP mitigates XSS even when escaping fails
HSTS prevents SSL stripping downgrade attacks

description: Enforce RBAC or ABAC on every protected endpoint
rationale: Checking auth once at login is insufficient — check per-request

description: Run npm audit or equivalent in CI and block on high/critical
rationale: Known CVEs in transitive deps are a common attack vector

description: Review OWASP Top 10 categories during code review
rationale: OWASP Top 10 is the industry-standard threat checklist

description: Grant the minimum permissions required, nothing more
rationale: Least privilege limits lateral movement after compromise

description: Apply strict rate limits on authentication endpoints
rationale: Unlimited auth endpoints enable credential stuffing

description: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags on all session cookies
rationale: These flags block common session hijacking vectors

description: Never log passwords, tokens, full PANs, or unredacted PII
rationale: Logs are often replicated and retained beyond application boundaries
